name: Newton
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Newton, KS 2026
seo_desc: Christmas events for kids in Newton, Kansas for 2026: a parade of lights, Five Places of Christmas and Gingy the gingerbread man, checked on host sites.
lede: Newton spreads its Christmas across a month of Saturdays downtown, with a lighted parade, a tree lighting at Depot Park and a free open house at five museums and historic sites.
celebrates: Choose Newton, the city's tourism group, anchors the season with Merry Little Main Street, a run of Saturdays from November 7 to December 19 that includes a free Christmas craft, a youth makers market, Window Wonderland, Small Business Saturday, Five Places of Christmas, festive photo booths and free gift wrapping. The Newton Community Christmas Tree is lit at Depot Park, where families sing carols and hear The Polar Express read aloud. The Newton Lions Club Parade of Lights comes down Main Street, and a Holiday Light Map invites residents to submit displays for others to find.
lastyear: The Newton chamber's Seven Saturdays of Christmas ran every Saturday from November 8 through December 20, 2025, with local shops and businesses hosting special events and a puzzle board with a grand prize drawing. Choose Newton's posts say Five Places of Christmas was held on December 6, 2025, at Warkentin House Museum, Harvey County Historical Museum, Kauffman Museum and Bethel College. A newer Light Up the Night event on November 21 added a community tree lighting for 2026.
facts: Newton's railroad roots run deep. The first Santa Fe depot was built in 1871 and the first train stopped there on July 17, 1871, and the original town was platted at the end of that August, according to Choose Newton's history page. Military Park is home to the Newton Public Library and Santa Fe steam locomotive No. 1880, which the Santa Fe Railroad donated to the city in 1955, according to the City of Newton. The Harvey County Historical Museum keeps an archive pamphlet on Engine 1880.
trains: Newton is a real railroad town. Santa Fe steam locomotive No. 1880 stands in Military Park downtown and can be seen from outside the fence. Amtrak's Southwest Chief stops at the Newton station, according to Amtrak, and the Harvey County Historical Museum at 203 N Main keeps more of the railroad story. For a bigger train day, the Great Plains Transportation Museum in Wichita is open Saturdays, according to our museum page.

faq: Newton celebrates with Merry Little Main Street Saturdays downtown from November 7 to December 19, a community tree lighting at Depot Park, the Newton Lions Club Parade of Lights and Five Places of Christmas, according to Choose Newton.
Where can kids see a Newton Christmas parade?

The Parade of Lights comes down Main Street in downtown Newton, hosted by the Newton Lions Club. Floats are decked out in Christmas lights, and Choose Newton says there is hot cocoa and pictures with Santa afterward.
What is Five Places of Christmas?

It is an annual free open house at five Newton and North Newton sites, among them Warkentin House Museum, Harvey County Historical Museum, Carriage Factory Art Gallery, Kauffman Museum and the Goerz House, with refreshments, giveaways and activities.
Can we see Christmas lights in Newton?
Yes. Choose Newton runs a Holiday Light Map of resident-submitted displays and says it is free to use.
Is there a train to see in Newton?
Yes. Santa Fe steam locomotive No. 1880 is on display in Military Park, and Amtrak's Southwest Chief stops at the Newton station.
